new_result.statement: For every symmetric block matrix with invertible k-by-k pivot B, including singular ambient A, the Schur complement S satisfies N_S(t)>=N_A(t)-k and s_j(S)>=s_{j+k}(A). The loss k is uniformly sharp for every pivot signature even when ||B|| tends to zero and A is singular.

exact_family.data: J=diag(I_p,-I_q), B=eps J, C=sqrt(eps) I_k, D=J
exact_family.consequence: S=0; A has p eigenvalues 1+eps, q eigenvalues -(1+eps), and k zeros. Thus N_A(1)=k and N_S(1)=0 while ||B||=eps.

compiler_interface.statement: In the reviewed s9 compiler, all Schur branches require fewer than nine ambient large directions; nine is imposed by the no-pivot Fourier endpoint.
compiler_interface.next_obligation: Any s9-to-s8 improvement must repair the no-pivot endpoint rather than seek a Schur-count refund.

retained_corrections: After zero-weight rows are omitted in the projection lemma, sum_i(1-b_i)<=d, not equality.
The notation A/B should be explicitly defined as the Schur complement.
continuity_status: Not audited as part of this lens; unrestricted continuity remains open.
open_status: The s8 endpoint and the unrestricted three-eigenvalue conjecture remain open.
